correctness.rationale: For a triangle, its three cyclic gaps must each be at most 2 or at least n−2. When n≥7 they cannot all be at most 2, so one is n−2 and the other two are 1. This identifies the complex with tight triple-cycle independence. Kim–Kim explicitly use mod two in §1; their Theorem 3.1 with k=3 gives the stated unique degree, and universal coefficients bound rational Betti numbers in that degree and kill the others. For augmentation, each chosen vertex orbit contributes a sign −1; the trace is (−1)^(d_n+1) times the weighted orbit assignments. Rotations repeat a bit word of length gcd(n,j); even for lengths 1 and 2 the periodic no-111 condition is encoded by closed walks of the stated two-bit transfer, whose spectrum is 0,1,i,−i. The identity trace gives rank, not an inference of torsion-freeness from mod two. A reflected word reduces to a path with two endpoint pairs forbidden from being 11: a fixed vertex is flanked by two copies of its neighbor bit, and an exchanged pair is flanked by its next inward bit. The remaining restrictions are exactly internal no-111. The weighted path count with the given start/end vectors has F(2)=F(3)=−1 and satisfies F(l+2)=−F(l) by the stated annihilation and Cayley–Hamilton. The three lengths and the prefactor give the traces in all four residue classes, including n=7 and the two even reflection axes. Averaging is not needed to identify the stated modules: the traces match the rational line and quarter-turn plane on every group element. Independent replay: python3 /workspace/review-evidence/reproduce.py 4, log /workspace/review-evidence/4.txt; graph triangles and 230 direct signed characters for 7≤n≤16, and independently built augmented mod-two boundary ranks through n=13. Finite checks corroborate the proof but do not establish general concentration. The supplied verifier and stored output were inspected, not executed.
